extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contains 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022, structured full texts, 210K figures, citation graphs, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. PDF files were processed using GROBID for full-text extraction and PDFFigures for figure extraction. Additional metadata and citation information were fetched using the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) API. The dataset undergoes annual updates by monitoring URL changes in the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The dataset is an unlabeled resource lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels. Some fields are only valid on a portion of the papers (e.g., only 16.8% of OCL papers have an arxiv_paper_id). Full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Metadata from the ACL Anthology website was used instead of extracted metadata for higher accuracy. Figures and tables were extracted separately. Citation networks were constructed using internal and external citation data from Semantic Scholar.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files were crawled. Full-text extraction was performed using GROBID. Figures were extracted using PDFFigures. Metadata was enriched using the Semantic Scholar API. Language detection was performed using a public toolkit. Topic labels were predicted using a supervised neural model (SPECTER) trained on a subset of 2,545 papers with ground truth labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were generated using a supervised neural model (SPECTER) trained on a curated dataset of 2,545 papers from conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021) with ground truth topics. These are referred to as 'silver-labeled' topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The topic classification was performed using a PLM-based supervised method (SPECTER) which achieved 69% accuracy. The system-predicted topics are considered silver data.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, Semantic Scholar API, SPECTER, SciBERT, BART-large-MNLI, langdetect
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates. The authors plan to update OCL by year to keep it up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus aims to advance open scientific research in Computational Linguistics, accelerate scientific progress, and promote reproducibility. It helps observe trends in the field, such as the waning interest in Syntax and the resurging interest in Natural Language Generation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is limited to the Computational Linguistics domain from the ACL Anthology. English is the most dominant language, with underrepresentation of other languages. The topic labels are biased towards dominant topics like Machine Translation in the top-cited papers analysis.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is small-scale and limited to peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology. It does not include other sources like arXiv. Full-text extraction quality is limited by the GROBID toolkit, with issues in extracting sections, footnotes, figures, and tables. The dataset lacks human annotations for specific tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Use cases include temporal topic trend analysis, document-level information extraction, section-wise tasks (related work generation), multimodal research (figure caption generation), pre-training scientific large language models, and knowledge graph construction.
